fixed.problem: Blocking 1 (review walk9): after Show older sessions, a session that ended while the Sessions tab was open made another session's row disappear. The heading read '23 sessions' over 22 rows, and Show older could not bring the row back. This broke ADR 0116 point 4 ('a session starting meanwhile never shifts or repeats a row') and design section 1 ('what the app says is true now').
fixed.failing_test_before: apps/ui/test/sessions-tab.test.tsx: 'after Show older sessions, a session that ends keeps every row on screen once, in order, and Show older goes on from the oldest shown' (45 ended + 1 working, 40 shown; failed with sess_19 missing) and 'with every session shown, one that ends makes the rows equal the count, and no Show older comes back' (the reviewer's 21 + 1 case). Both fail on 5450867's SessionsTab.tsx and pass after the fix.
fixed.how: apps/ui/src/pages/project/SessionsTab.tsx. Root cause: a re-read fetched only the first page and joined it to the older pages already on screen. The ended session joined the first page and pushed the old 20th row onto page two, which was in neither list. `next` stayed on the older page's cursor. Fix: once older pages are on screen (ShownTo = {id of the oldest row shown, the cursor its page gave after it}), a re-read reads on down to that row (limit 50 a request), cuts there and keeps that cursor. The daemon's keyset (created_at, id) never changes for an ended session, so the cursor stays valid. Every row on screen is read again, so each says what is true now. Reads run one after the other in a promise queue (a re-read and Show older never cross; one waiting re-read covers the others). A generation counter drops answers for a project left. With only the first page shown, it behaves as before (one request, the first page's own cursor). No daemon change: the route already takes `limit`.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Open a project with more than 20 sessions, More > Sessions, and press Show older sessions. Start a session (Start), watch its working row on top, then end it (Stop now on its page, or let it finish). The rows you saw stay, in order, with the ended session at the top. The heading's count equals the rows once every page is shown. With more than 40 sessions and two pages shown, Show older sessions is still offered and brings the rest, each session once, the project's first session last. Bench evidence: /tmp/frbench/fixup-d1109-sessions-evidence/walk2.json (22 + 1, all PASS), walk3-pages.json (43 + 1 with two pages shown: 40 rows kept, 41 after the end, Show older to 44 = the daemon's list in its order; 6 re-reads of one limit=50 request each, 2 Show older requests), screenshots in after-steps/01-03, 06, 08-11. Live check 4: same walk on a real project; also leave the tab open through a whole real session.

fixed.problem: Blocking 2 (review step 11): on a working session's page, 'Tasks in this session' showed the running task at 'Running CHF 0.00' for the whole run while 'Spent of this session's budget' grew. This was W15-21's 'CHF 0.00 until the run returns' on a new screen, and it broke SL-9 (each task row's CHF equals the ledger's sum for that session and task) and design section 3.7 (spend updated live).
fixed.failing_test_before: apps/ui/test/sessions-tab.test.tsx 'while the session works, the running task's CHF follows the session's spend, read at most once a second' (failed before: the row stayed at CHF 0.00 after the session.changed frame with the higher spend).
fixed.how: apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx. Root cause: GET /sessions/:id/tasks was read again only when the count of task.started/task.finished lines or the session's status changed. The daemon books every model call with its task, and the stream's session.changed carries the new spend, but the page never asked. Fix: while the session works, a change in session.spent.chfMicro reads the tasks again. A first change reads at once, later ones at most once a second (TASKS_READ_MS = 1000, the stream's pace); a frame that moves nothing reads nothing. A new session's page starts with no stale tasks (an AbortController and spendRead per id). I first built it with 5 s as the reviewer suggested (the Sessions tab's FRAME_READ_MS), but the bench showed a one-task session reading 'CHF 0.03' on the meter beside 'CHF 0.02' on its only task (walk1.json, failed check 'settled'). The two sit side by side on this page, so they now agree within a second (walk2.json: 8 of 8 samples match the daemon and the meter). Daemon-side companion test: apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts 'd1109-sessions, run C' > 'SL-9 while a task runs: …'. It holds the run's second model call (the describe's hold() gained an optional number of calls let through first) and checks that GET /sessions/:id/tasks answers 'Running' with the ledger's sum for the session and the task mid-run, equal to the session's spend, and the ledger's sum again at the end. It passed before too: the daemon was right, the page did not ask.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Start a session on a long task, open its page (from the header's working line or More > Sessions). Under 'Tasks in this session' the running task's CHF follows 'Spent of this session's budget' within about a second (for a one-task session the two read the same). After Stop now or the end, the row equals what the session spent on it. Bench evidence: after-steps/04-05 (Running CHF 0.02 beside CHF 0.02 of CHF 5.00), walk2.json samples. Live check 4 (LC-C5): on the real model, watch a task with several model calls: the task's CHF moves with each booked call and never stays at CHF 0.00 while the meter grows.
